_comment: Dependency index for documents that MUST STAY CURRENT. Each entry names the authoritative
sources a document was derived from, and the date it was last checked against them.
Checked by scripts/docs/check_doc_sources.py — when a source changes after a document's
'reviewed' date, that document is flagged as possibly stale. See CORE.md section 5.
DELIBERATELY NOT INDEXED: docs/decisions/ and docs/contracts/. Those are point-in-time
records and frozen interfaces — they are superseded, never refreshed, so a staleness flag
on them would be noise. See .ai/skills/docs-author/references/DESIGN-DOC.md.
'reviewed' is an attestation ('someone read this against its sources on this date'), not an
edit date. Fixing a typo does not advance it; re-checking the content against the sources does.

docs.note: Sign-in model and roster/auth rules from PROJECT.md; the 2359-night-before due date rule from CORE.md section 2; what the Lessons and Dashboard pages actually show from the student modules.

Student-facing promise about what AI does and does not decide. CORE.md section 6 governs 3-state grading, is_finalized=false, and the hidden diagnostics; the two skills define what actually gets written.
The 3-state toggle, question_scores shape, and the 'all my sections' scoping rule. If the Grade tab's behaviour changes, this doc is wrong before anything else is.
Says in-page that CORE.md and PROJECT.md remain authoritative and that this page is the bug if they disagree — so it is the entry most likely to need a refresh when the contract moves.
Summarises the shared-state rules and the operating contract. Must never contain what SYSTEM_GUIDE.md may contain — help docs are public at every tier.
The authoring contract. Documents the renderer's actual behaviour — tier gating, the manifest fields, the no-front-matter Jekyll trap. Not served to users.
Course-director and system operating guide. Roles, edge functions, and admin procedures are defined in PROJECT.md and must agree.

The ordered PREP v2 cutover procedure. Derived step-for-step from the bootstrap SQL (roles, auth-FK, read window, seal) and the migration script (what moves, what is left behind, the frozen-slug check). If either changes, the runbook is wrong before anything else.

Encodes the help-doc mechanics (no front matter, start at ##, manifest fields, tier gating) and the docs/ taxonomy. If the renderer or the taxonomy changes, the skill teaches the wrong thing to every future author.

Conceptual companion to director-schema-reference.md, which owns the field-level detail and the enforced-rules list; this page links out rather than restating them, after a restated unlock rule drifted and contradicted the reference. Deliberately contains no UI procedures - site/app/ does not read the app schema yet.

Every table and field transcribed from the app-schema migrations and verified against information_schema on the live database. Owns the enforced-rules list and the exact accepted values. Inline SVG depends on the .sf-* classes in styles.css. Omits RLS policy predicates - help docs are world-readable at every tier.
